subject: Standard-binary arithmetic
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.4 'the equivalent arithmetic expression is defined by the implementor'` -> OK (§8.8.1.4.4 rule 2, sub-item e). Expected behavior: for a positive exponent, integer exponents 1/2/3/4 have PINNED expansions (x; x*x; (x*x)*x; (x*x)*(x*x)) -- note d) is (x*x)*(x*x), not ((x*x)*x)*x, and the difference is observable in binary floating point because each multiplication rounds; every other positive exponent is implementor-defined but must be developed over SBIDI operands with each +,-,*,/ obeying ISO/IEC 60559:2020. READ: NumericRenderer.Power (NumericRenderer.cs:544-553) routes only `StandardDecimal` (= StandardDecimal or Standard, NumericRenderer.cs:559) to RuntimeApi.DecPow/CobolDec.Pow, whose header comment (NumericRenderer.cs:546-551) documents exactly this rule shape for the SDIDI twin: 'an integer exponent evaluates by repeated SDIDI multiplication (r2a-r2d exactly; r2e's implementor-defined form for larger integers ...)' citing §8.8.1.5.4. There is NO SBIDI counterpart: no ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary arm in Power, no SBIDI carrier in src (grep for SBIDI / the NOTE 3 range constants: nothing), and the mode is rejected at bind (DataBinder.cs:318-320, COBOL0806, unconditional per EditionContext.cs:109). Sub-item e) is an A.1-style implementor-defined element INSIDE an unimplemented facility, so it is not a separable NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION -- there is no expression to define because there is no mode. All five sub-items unimplemented; not a PARTIAL. Editions 2014,2023 (F.2 item 3 / E.2 item 21 derivation, not from ConstructRegistry). WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: an SBIDI Pow whose 1/2/3/4 legs emit the exact association the rule prints (a golden distinguishing (x*x)*(x*x) from ((x*x)*x)*x on a value where the roundings differ), plus a documented choice for e) recorded in CONFORMANCE.md. || UPHELD: I re-ran the citation myself -- `python scripts/spec/cite.py --check 8.8.1.4.4 'the equivalent arithmetic expression is defined by the implementor'` -> `OK  §8.8.1.4.4 2) b)  (Exponentiation in standard-binary arithmetic)` (the locator prints the enclosing rule 2's sub-item indexing; the matched line is sub-item e as quoted). I read §8.8.1.4.4 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:7988-8038 and confirm the association the adjudicator flags: sub-item c) is '((operand-1 * operand-1) * operand-1)' and sub-item d) is '((operand-1 * operand-1) * (operand-1 * operand-1))' -- d) is the balanced tree, and under 60559 rounding that is observably different from a left-associated chain, so a future implementation cannot substitute a repeated-multiply loop for it. I also verified the NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION question the adjudicator disposed of: sub-item e is implementor-defined, but §4.2.5 makes implementor definition apply only 'to required normative elements ... and to optional language elements for which an implementor claims support' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:2128) -- support is not claimed here, so there is nothing to decide separately and NOT-IMPLEMENTED is correct rather than NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. Line refs corrected as on GR-8.8.1.4.4-1 (Power at :543, StandardDecimal at :394). || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
